html:
Lata Mangeshkar was the leading singer of Indian film music for more than half a century. Hers is probably the most heard voice in the history of the subcontinent.

She was born in 1929 at Indore, the eldest child of a classical singer who ran a travelling theatre company. He died when she was thirteen, and she went to work as a child actor and singer to feed her mother, brother and three sisters.

Indian films are full of songs, and the actors do not sing them. A "playback" singer records the song and the actor mouths it. Film producers at first found her voice too thin. In 1949 her song in the film Mahal, "Aayega Aanewala", made her famous. From then into the 1990s she was the singing voice of almost every leading actress, from one generation to the next. She recorded thousands of songs in more than thirty languages. Her sister Asha Bhosle was her only rival.

In January 1963, weeks after the war with China, she sang a song for the dead soldiers in Delhi. Nehru was moved to tears.

She fought for singers to be paid royalties and named on records. She received the Bharat Ratna, India's highest honour, in 2001. When she died in 2022 the country held two days of mourning.
sum: Lata Mangeshkar was the leading singer of Indian film music for more than half a century. Hers is probably the most heard voice in the history of the subcontinent.
